headline: Your Cupix waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing construction firms into the right Cupix spatial-intelligence offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Jérémie Henry.
productSummary: Cupix is a spatial intelligence platform for construction and facility management. Teams walk a site with a consumer-grade 360 camera. Cupix AI turns that video into a 4D digital twin they can measure, annotate, and compare against BIM over time. SiteInsights, the add-on, aligns those captures with BIM and the schedule so completion is calculated across work areas, trades, and BIM categories. The all-in-one spatial hub unifies 360 maps, laser scans, drone orthos, and BIM in one georeferenced model. Integrates with Autodesk BIM360, ACC, Autodesk Forma, Procore, Revizto, Oracle, and ArcGIS. Homepage: join thousands of global leaders across construction, oil and gas, manufacturing, and government.
coreInsight: Jérémie already sells spatial intelligence so builders and operators can see the site without flying there. Sophia's original pitch is the TAM: scrape construction firms, write to PMs and Owners who need visibility across the building lifecycle. The one list is construction firms LinkedIn already lists. The one routing signal is the job-keyword class in their open reqs, because Sales Nav returns that keyword in the same pull and it tells you whether they are staffing BIM/VDC progress, a capture stack, facilities handover, or none of those yet. PM and Owner titles are the people layer after the firm is routed. They are not a second TAM.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the keyword already in the job post
sections.takeaway: LinkedIn already names the construction firm and already prints BIM, VDC, reality capture, or facilities handover in the open req. That keyword is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every construction firm
sections.takeaway: First match wins. BIM/VDC/progress keywords go first, then reality-capture keywords, then facilities/handover keywords, then every remaining in-TAM construction firm.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each job keyword gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: BIM/VDC hiring gets a SiteInsights progress-gap brief. Capture-stack hiring gets a spatial-hub stack map. Facilities/handover hiring gets a lifecycle record. The rest get the 20-minute walk playbook Brandt Companies already proved.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Catch the delay, unify the scans, hand over a record, skip the flight
sections.takeaway: The list is always construction firms, aimed at PMs, Owners, VDC/BIM leads, and facilities managers. Project type is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the req they already posted
sections.takeaway: Notice the keyword, poke the walk-and-spreadsheet gap that keyword implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the BIM/VDC keyword first
sections.takeaway: Start where they are already staffing the model-versus-field gap SiteInsights is built for. Prove reply density, then roll capture-stack, handover, and the 20-minute-walk catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn Sales Nav job search is the TAM Sophia already named, construction firms with a visible PM or Owner, and the spatial-intelligence keyword in one pull.

The same pull returns BIM / VDC / progress tracking / 4D, laser / LiDAR / drone / Matterport / OpenSpace / 360, or facilities / handover / as-built operations, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Cupix copy: SiteInsights (needs BIM, large jobs), the all-in-one spatial hub (laser, drone, 360, BIM in one model), the 4D as-built record for operators, and the 360-walk that cut Brandt Companies' weekly field report from 3 hours to 20 minutes.
PM, Owner, project type, and title are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

sources.name: LinkedIn Sales Navigator job search
sources.delivers: Construction firms plus the open-req keyword used to assign Tier 1 / 2 / 3 / catch-all. The TAM gate and the spine of every route. One pull.

sources.name: Company careers / jobs page scrape
sources.delivers: Posted role text when Sales Nav truncates the keyword, plus project_type as a merge tag when the req names a hospital, data center, factory, hotel, or multifamily job

sources.name: LinkedIn company + title graph
sources.delivers: Project Manager, Owner, Project Executive, Superintendent, VDC / BIM Manager, Director of Construction, Facilities Manager after the domain is routed. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM.

sources.name: Optional Dodge / ConstructConnect project index

sources.name: Apollo (after qualification)

sources.name: Optional Cupix customer suppress

routingRules.why: Already a customer. Named case-study logos on cupix.com are not enough to exclude every office.

Open req names reality capture, laser scan, LiDAR, drone, photogrammetry, Matterport, OpenSpace, StructionSite, HoloBuilder, 360 camera, or point cloud, and no bim_vdc keyword. Class estimated.

Remaining construction firms LinkedIn already lists: visible PM / Owner / superintendent / director of construction, and none of the keywords above

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: BIM / VDC keyword
tiers.trigger: LinkedIn job post names BIM, VDC, digital twin, progress tracking, 4D schedule, model manager, look-ahead, percent complete, or as-built verification. Keyword class estimated, not a Cupix site field.
tiers.pain: They are staffing the model. Percent-complete still comes from a walk and a spreadsheet, so BIM and the field disagree until someone is on site. SiteInsights FAQ: you have to have BIM models for the AI to measure progress. Best on large jobs with a lot of ground to cover: data centers, factories, hospitals, multifamily, hotels.
tiers.valueProp: SiteInsights aligns 360 captures, BIM, and the schedule and calculates completion across work areas, trades, and BIM categories. Progress-tracking page: 7 million BIM elements tracked, 70 projects using SiteInsights since January 2025, 450 million+ square feet captured. Ramsay, Head of Innovation, Built, on that page: selected Cupix to capture construction site progress and integrate 3D models with the physical world. Muhammad Khalil Bin Shaiful Bahar, Boustead Projects: look at site progress, identify discrepancies, validate as-built progress with AI.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already budgeted a role to keep the model honest against the field.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Reality-capture keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names reality capture, laser scan, LiDAR, drone, photogrammetry, Matterport, OpenSpace, StructionSite, HoloBuilder, 360 camera, or point cloud, and no bim_vdc keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: They already capture. Laser lives in one app, drone in another, 360 in a third, BIM somewhere else. Homepage: the complexity of multiple applications. Spatial-hub page: unify 360, laser scans, and drone imagery in one georeferenced source of truth.
tiers.valueProp: Cupix all-in-one spatial hub brings 360 maps, laser scans, drone orthos, and BIM into one coordinated twin. Spatial-hub page: tens of billions of points, EPSG georeferencing, BIM deviation, Matterport and ArcGIS integrations. Mitch Medway, Regional Digital Lead, Arcadis: Cupix has a nice synergy with the Autodesk ecosystem they already invested in globally.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already pay for capture. The silo is the pain the hub is built for.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Facilities / handover keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names facilities manager, building operations, handover, turnover package, as-built documentation, owner's rep, CAFM, IWMS, or facility digital twin, and no bim_vdc or reality_capture keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: The job is leaving construction and entering operations. Homepage: record spatial changes for full accountability, frequent 360 walks replace thousands of photos, a complete 4D record. John Holland customer-story page: close out with a 3D record that holds up at handover and beyond. Coquitlam customer-story page: fragmented facility data, repeat site visits, coordination across departments.
tiers.valueProp: Cupix keeps the 4D as-built as the handover asset, not a binder of photos. Homepage industries include construction and facility management. Coquitlam story: remote access, fewer site visits, Canadian Network of Asset Managers Innovation Award. Spatial-hub page: as-built quality check with 360, laser, and BIM in one place.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. They are already staffing the operator side of Sophia's lifecycle pitch.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM construction firm: visible PM, Owner, superintendent, or director of construction, and none of the keywords above.
tiers.pain: They are still in the builder-and-operator set Sophia named. Understanding the site still means a flight. Homepage: give the entire team spatial understanding remotely, eliminate miscommunication, prevent rework, make decisions without site visits.
tiers.valueProp: Walk with a 360 camera. Cupix turns the video into a 4D twin. Brandt Companies on the 360-to-3D-map page: more than 80% of their time on sites for documentation. Breanne Hanson, Senior Engineer, Brandt Companies: weekly field report from 3 hours to a 20-minute walk a less experienced partner can do. Homepage: 70% time and efficiency gains. Korean homepage copy: 80%+ time versus traditional video documentation.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: 20-Minute Walk Playbook
campaigns.filter: Remaining in-TAM construction firms, job_keyword_class = none
campaigns.strategy: Notice the construction firm LinkedIn already lists, name the flight-to-understand-the-site gap Sophia pitched, offer the 20-minute walk Brandt Companies already runs
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped construction firm still gets one route. The playbook is the tiny yes.

campaigns.name: 70% homepage variant
campaigns.strategy: Lead with 70% time and efficiency gains on the homepage, average reduction in site visits, reporting time, and design iterations. Do not change routing.

launchPlan: Pull LinkedIn Sales Nav for construction firms with a visible Project Manager, Owner, Project Executive, Superintendent, VDC / BIM Manager, Director of Construction, or Facilities Manager, or with construction / project-engineer jobs. Keep the open-req keyword in the same export. Classify job_keyword_class as bim_vdc, reality_capture, facilities_ops, or none. Suppress already_customer when a Cupix deployment is visible. Named case-study logos (Built, Brandt, Boustead, Arcadis, John Holland, Coquitlam, BNBuilders, Naylor Love) are not a blanket exclude.

Keyword classes are estimated GTMx taxonomy, not Cupix site fields. Tune the synonym list after the first Sales Nav pull if a band is starved or overlapping. First match wins. Do not also route on Dodge project value or headcount. Those cutoffs are not on cupix.com.

Resolve work emails in Apollo only after the domain is routed. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM. Optional Dodge / ConstructConnect and careers-page text fill {{project_type}} (hospital, data center, factory, hotel, multifamily) as a merge tag only.

Launch Tier 1 SiteInsights Progress Gap Brief first. Smallest list, sharpest BIM-versus-field signal, closest to SiteInsights (needs BIM, large jobs). Discrepancy copy as the control, 7 million elements as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 Spatial Hub Stack Map once {{named_keyword}} merge tags are clean across laser, drone, Matterport, and OpenSpace language. Then Tier 3 Lifecycle Handover Record.

Turn on the 20-Minute Walk Playbook catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM construction firm still has a route. That is Sophia's original PM / Owner visibility pitch. Keep project_type as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one job-keyword tier is clearly working. Do not launch a tier under about 1,500 contacts. That threshold is the waterfall SOP, not a Cupix site number.

thresholds.action: Perfect. Scale that tier. Keep the winning discrepancy, stack, handover, or walk variant.

Borderline. Swap only the magnet or the first-line job keyword. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: Worse than 1 per 500, or reply rate under 1% after 1,500+ sends
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall. Retune the estimated bim_vdc / reality_capture / facilities_ops synonym lists from the live scrape if a band is starved of contacts.
